extracted.intended_audience: university faculty researchers applying for NSERC Discovery Grants (Canada), research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and selection criteria for preparing and submitting an individual Discovery Grants (DG) application to NSERC, including eligibility, application materials, reviewer suggestions, and how proposals and HQP training are assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific or engineering excellence of the researcher
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessed on the researcher's knowledge, expertise and experience; quality of contributions to and impact on the proposed and other areas of research in the natural sciences and engineering; importance of contributions to, and use by, other researchers and end-users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members evaluate knowledge, expertise, experience, the quality and impact of contributions, and how other researchers or end-users use those contributions. This is one of the selection criteria determining the overall merit rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which the proposal suggests and explores novel or potentially transformative concepts and lines of inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should highlight novel ideas and transformative potential of the proposed research within the summary and application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance and expected contributions (impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance and expected contributions to research; potential for policy and/or technology-related impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate the expected contributions to the field and potential broader impacts in policy or technology where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and scope of objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity and scope of objectives — proposal should describe a research program with long-term goals rather than a single short-term project or collection of projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are for ongoing programs of research; clearly state long-term goals and how proposed activities fit within a sustained research program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and appropriateness of methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity and appropriateness of the methodology proposed to achieve the research objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient methodological detail to show that approaches are appropriate for the questions and objectives; clarity affects assessment of feasibility and merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Feasibility of the proposed research program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address practical considerations, timelines, resource requirements and whether the proposed methods can realistically achieve stated objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope addresses relevant issues and needed expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which the scope of the proposal addresses all relevant issues, including the need for varied expertise within or across disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If varied expertise is required, describe how it will be incorporated (collaborators, team composition, interdisciplinary methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of equity, diversity and inclusion (research process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of equity, diversity and inclusion in the research process where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how EDI considerations are integrated into the research design and processes where relevant; NSERC values EDI as foundational to research quality and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of interdisciplinary methods or practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of interdisciplinary methods or practices in research, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For interdisciplinary research, ensure appropriate EG members and external reviewers are identified; refer to Guidelines for the Preparation and Review of Applications in Interdisciplinary Research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness and justification of the budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of, and justification for, the budget requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget must be justified relative to the program of research; applicants should show why requested resources are necessary and how they will be used in accordance with the Tri-agency Guide on Financial Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of conceptual distinctness from CIHR/SSHRC-funded research
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstration that the DG proposal is conceptually distinct from research support held or applied for through CIHR and/or SSHRC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must show the program of research is within NSERC's mandate (NSE other than health) and conceptually distinct from CIHR/SSHRC-support; otherwise the application may be rejected or directed to other programs (e.g., Discovery Horizons for inter-agency interdisciplinary work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to the training of highly qualified personnel (HQP) — overall
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of quality and impact of past training of HQP and the quality, suitability and clarity of the planned training of HQP (training philosophy and research training plan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall HQP rating combines assessment of past contributions and future training plan. The onus is on applicants to provide sufficient detail and evidence so members can assess both past impact and proposed activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: HQP training plan — research training plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Research training plan should provide details on the activities or projects in which research personnel will be involved and how these relate to achieving objectives; must show activities appropriate to the level of research personnel (undergraduate, Masters, PhD, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient detail so reviewers can judge appropriateness for each trainee level and how the activities will contribute to objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: HQP training plan — training philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Training philosophy should describe approach to interaction with HQP, research mentorship methods, opportunities provided, intellectual involvement of HQP, skills and knowledge HQP will acquire, expected impact, and plans to promote participation of a diverse group of HQP (including EDI challenges and specific actions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starting in 2020 the training philosophy must include a qualitative description of EDI challenges/barriers and specific actions to promote participation of diverse HQP. Describe mentorship methods and how trainees will gain skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past contributions to HQP — training environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of past training environment: participation and involvement of HQP in training and development opportunities such as outreach, interdisciplinary research, promoting EDI, collaborations and interactions with private/public sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss type and nature of training and development opportunities, describe challenges/barriers and actions taken to support EDI; trainee demographic data is not requested nor required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past contributions to HQP — HQP awards and research contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that HQP have collaborated in research contributions (conferences, publications, patents, technical reports, etc.), which can indicate intellectual involvement and success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples such as co-authorship, awards and research outputs; norms vary by discipline — explain context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past contributions to HQP — outcomes and skills gained
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of progression of HQP into further studies or impactful careers and how skills gained are being used in their careers or further studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes can be in private sector, public sector or academia and may be NSE or non-NSE domains; clearly demonstrate how skills gained were applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: HQP assessment rules and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules include: HQP trained entirely outside the six-year window are not considered except for eligible leaves; mentorship is not considered official supervision; general teaching responsibilities are not assessed under HQP criterion; all HQP must be identified by an asterisk; presentations by HQP can be included as evidence; academic advisor role typically not counted as official supervisor in CCV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide names where possible; if names cannot be obtained provide anonymized sufficient info; explain roles when co-supervisor; members avoid quantifying by numbers and focus on quality and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOI (Notification of Intent) mandatory
rubrics_metrics.description: A notification of intent to apply (NOI) is a mandatory step; applicants who do not submit an NOI will not be able to submit a full application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOI enables NSERC to begin review preparation (EG assignment, selection of external reviewers, subject matter eligibility verification). Follow the Research Portal instructions and attach NSERC CCV to NOI.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSERC Canadian Common CV (CCV) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must complete and submit the NSERC version of the Canadian Common CV (CCV) at both NOI and full application stages; CCV must be in same language as application; names and email used to create CCV account must match Research Portal account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CCV can be updated between NOI and full application but updates must be made prior to full application submission. Ensure platform language consistency if saving in French versus English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of proposal content and length
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary of proposal must not exceed 6,000 characters and should: state objectives of the proposed research program; summarize the scientific approach; highlight the novelty and expected significance of the work to a field(s) in the natural sciences and engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep within 6,000 characters and include these three elements clearly. If your program changes substantially between NOI and full application, contact the program officer for the EG you selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: External reviewer suggestions (mandatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide five external reviewers who: are not in a conflict of interest; are not from the applicant's institution; are from different institutions from one another; can provide an independent assessment; are capable of reviewing in the language of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraged to suggest diverse reviewers (Canadian, international, established and early-career, women and other underrepresented groups, academic and non-academic). Do not contact suggested reviewers. Avoid proposing reviewers affiliated with a Named Research Organization (NRO) if research aims to advance a Sensitive Technology Research Area (STRA). NSERC will not select members currently serving on an NSERC evaluation group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest guidelines for external reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: A conflict of interest may be deemed to exist or be perceived when reviewers: are a relative or close friend; have a financial/material interest in the funding outcome; have long-standing scientific or personal differences; are currently affiliated with applicant's institutions/organizations/companies; are closely professionally affiliated due to frequent and regular interactions within last six years; have been a supervisor or trainee; collaborated, published or shared funding with the applicant or have plans to; have been employed by the institution; feel unable to provide an impartial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSERC reserves the right to resolve uncertainties and determine if a conflict exists. Refer to the Conflict of interest and confidentiality policy of the federal research funding organizations for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: individual faculty and appointment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must meet NSERC's Individual eligibility (for university faculty). If an offer of a position is pending at time of application, the faculty position must be taken up no later than September 1 of the year of the grant before any funds can be released and must be confirmed in writing to NSERC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjunct professors have a specific 'Access to funds by adjunct professors' section. Researchers can apply only if they meet eligibility rules; verify eligibility before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on holding Discovery Grants and program overlaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers can apply for and hold only one DG at a time; those who currently hold a DG cannot reapply for another until the last year of their current award. Applicants cannot simultaneously hold a Discovery Grant and a Discovery Horizons grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual may submit LOIs to both Discovery Horizons and the DG NOI stage, but must choose one program before submitting a full application (full application may be submitted only to one program).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter eligibility and mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must present a program of research eligible under NSERC's mandate: to promote and assist research in the natural sciences and engineering (other than health). The application will be rejected if NSERC determines subject matter is outside its mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Selecting the Appropriate Federal Granting Agency, Addendum to guidelines for eligibility of applications related to health, Peer Review Manual, and NSERC Discovery Grants Process for Decisions on Mandate Eligibility for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible funding use and Tri-agency financial rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery Grants provide long-term operating funds and are considered 'grants in aid'—they are not meant to support full costs of a research program. All expenditures are subject to the principles and directives in the Tri-agency Guide on Financial Administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSERC encourages obtaining funds from other sources (not CIHR/SSHRC) to support full costs as long as those funds cover different expenses from those in the DG application.

rubrics_metrics.name: STRAC Policy and Sensitive Technology Research Areas (STRA) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must identify whether their proposed research aims to advance a sensitive technology research area. If so, submission of attestation forms will be required from researchers with named roles to certify they are not affiliated with, nor receiving funding/in-kind support from, a Named Research Organization (NRO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the STRAC Policy and Tri-agency guidance on STRAC for procedures, responsibilities of researchers and institutions, and additional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and assessment process and decision rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are submitted to the DG program and reviewed by Evaluation Groups (EGs) comprising Canadian and international peers; there may be external reviewer input. The overall merit assessment is based on combination of ratings by the EG for each selection criterion; final rating and applicant category determine grant level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At NOI stage applicants suggest an EG; NSERC reserves final assignment. For interdisciplinary research EG membership and external reviewers will be selected to ensure appropriate review.

rubrics_metrics.name: HQP six‑year window and leave accommodation
rubrics_metrics.description: HQP trained entirely outside the six-year window will not be considered in evaluation of past contributions to HQP training. Applicants with eligible leaves of absence may include supplemental contributions from their most recent active research period prior to the last six years for a period equivalent to the duration of the leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to application instructions for details on eligible leaves and how to include supplemental contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission and deadlines rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted via the Research Portal; NOI must be submitted by NOI deadline to enable full application. Full applications must be received by NSERC by 8:00 pm (ET) on the deadline date or they will be rejected. Once submitted, an application cannot be updated or modified before or after the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional internal deadlines apply—submit to your institution's research grants office by their internal deadline. In systems interruptions consult the Service standards policy on sustained interruptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: External reviewer exclusion requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may request that some researchers, organizations or large collaborations not be involved in review; NSERC will take this into consideration but cannot be bound by it. NSERC may also exclude reviewers because of conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that exclusion type 'Collaboration' refers to large research groups. Information concerning exclusions may be accessible to those individuals named under the Privacy Act.
